approvalTitle: requirements.md: converting the Ansible structure diagram to DISL and FBL
content:
# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The user's request, verbatim (2026-10-09):

> Create spec workflow MCP specifications. One specification for converting one of the standalone diagram tools to FBL and DISL. i.e. analyse the current implementation, define the DISL and FBL and then write the specification on the refactoring., also focus on finding issues and aspects where the DISL and FBL languages do not yet cover everything.

This is one of the fifteen specifications that reading gives (the series and the survey behind it are in `causal-loop-disl-fbl`, *Introduction*). It converts the **Ansible structure diagram** (`ansible/structure`, module folder `ansible-structure`), a tool on neither language.

**Two things were established first, because they decide what a conversion of this tool is.**

1. **The tool never writes its subject.** Its subject is a folder: playbooks, roles, inventories, `ansible.cfg` and Jinja templates. `AnsibleProjectReader` opens nothing for writing, the module registers no document factory, no toolbox provider, no context action provider and no command handler (`ServiceCollection.AddAnsibleStructure.cs`), and `ZeroWrites.Tests` holds the fixture trees byte for byte and by modification time. The one write is a dragged node's position, into the `layout:` block of the `.adp` registration, through core's `SetRegistrationLayoutCommand`. So there is no insert, no remove and no splice to specify: the conversion is **reading, derivation and the registration**.
2. **The folder is read by a persistence plugin (FBL section 11) inside a declared folder subject (FBL section 10), not by declared rules.** FBL 11.5 names "Ansible project folders" among the formats expected to stay plugins, and finding B1 confirms it against the reader: what the tool recognises is folders, file counts and an INI inventory, none of which is an entry of a YAML file. What FBL section 10 declares, and the host then does instead of the module, is everything around the reading: which files are read, the settle delay, watching, that nothing is written, and the registration. The findings of table B are therefore about the folder subject and the plugin contract.

**What "converted" means here** is what `causal-loop-disl-fbl` says, less what a read-only tool has not got: the property rows, the findings and the refusals are derived from a bundled DISL definition by `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl`; the folder is selected, watched and handed over as an FBL folder subject by `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl`; and the module keeps the plugin and what neither language can state.

## What was measured

Read on 2026-10-09: the module at `develop` `9a646009`; `definitions/diagrams/ansible-structure.dis` and `.md`, the DISL specification (0.3 draft) and the FBL specification (0.2 draft) in etalii-adp/etalii.adp at `develop` `da64ff0`; and the two libraries in this repository.

| Thing | State |
| --- | --- |
| The module's backend | 3,445 lines of C# in 41 files. `AnsibleProjectReader` (605 lines) and `AnsibleYaml` (88) read the folder with YamlDotNet; `AnsibleGraph` (307) resolves the relations; `AnsibleRuleSet` (163) and `AnsibleValidator` (98) hold the five findings; `AnsibleContextPropertyProvider` (360) holds the rows; `AnsibleLayout` (155) arranges. 15 test files and four fixture trees. |
| The module's client | 588 lines. `AnsibleCanvas.tsx` (391) holds a hand-written canvas definition. |
| The DISL definition | Exists in etalii.adp, 728 lines, **written against DISL 0.1**. It is not bundled here (`src/diagrams/ansible-structure/definition/` does not exist). It names a plugin as its persistence format. |
| The FBL binding | None exists. FBL 11.5 and section 17 expect a plugin reader; the example to follow is `helm-chart.fbl`, the other read-only folder subject. The appendix drafts one. |
| The real-file check | None. `RealFiles/divergences.json` has no entry that names this tool, and `ModuleCrossCheck.Tests` does not read it. |
| The corpus | Four fixture trees, the module's `examples/` (25 files) and `src/examples/diagrams/ansible-structure/` (345 files, 12 registrations, 6 of them with a `layout:` block holding 34 stored positions). |
| A parity transcript | None. |

**How each finding is known:** *measured* is a search of this repository or of the specification text, whose command is in *Sources*; *read* is a reading of the code against the specification text, not run; *recorded* would be an entry of `divergences.json` or a test, and this tool has none. Nothing was built or run. Requirement 1 turns every *read* finding into a fixture before anything is changed.

## Findings

The three kinds are those of `causal-loop-disl-fbl`: a **definition defect** is repaired in the definition or the binding, a **runtime gap** in this repository's libraries, a **language gap** in etalii-adp/etalii.adp. A **behaviour change to rule on** becomes an open question.

### A. The DISL definition against the module

| # | Finding | Kind | Known |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | The definition is DISL 0.1 (`"disl": "0.1"`). The client's `parseDisl` refuses anything but 0.3. It must be rewritten at 0.3 before it can be bundled. | Definition defect | Measured |
| A2 | Its companion lists twelve things "DISL 0.1 could not express". Eight are answered since: a relation with no target (an `optional` target end drawn as a `stub`, for which DISL 4.9 uses `UsesRole` as its own example), a reason on every read-only row (`readOnlyReasons`), a finding at a file and line and one finding per item (`location`, `forEach`), formula ids (the `derived` id strategy with an `expression`), `color-mix` (`color().mix()`), and, from FBL, the folder as subject, view data outside the subject and re-reading on change (FBL 10, 8.3, 10.3). The reported rule ids are `code`, not `x-adp-ruleId`; the origin is `language.origin`, not `x-adp.origin`. Four stay: recognition and reading (B1), relation resolution (B1), the ranked layout (A14) and revealing a file (A13). | Definition defect | Read |
| A3 | The definition invents a node type, `UnresolvedTarget`, one per unresolved relation "with the relation's id", so that a relation always has a target. The module keeps the relation with an empty target and draws a stub. With an `optional` target the type goes, and with it an element that shares an id with its relation. | Definition defect | Read |
| A4 | `persistence` names `plugin:net.etalii.adp.ansible.folder` as the format, with `encoding` and `metadata`. It becomes `format: "fbl"` with `binding`, and DISL 11.2 forbids those two keys beside a binding. The plugin stays declared, as the binding's reader. | Definition defect | Read |
| A5 | The id strategy is `natural` with type prefixes. DISL 11.5.1 composes a natural id from the prefix and the `key` attributes, and a play's only key is `indexInPlaybook`, so every first play of every playbook would be `play:0`. The module's id is `play:` followed by the playbook's path, `#` and the index. Relation ids (`edge:`, the source id, the kind and the target as written, joined by a vertical bar) are not stated at all. Each is a `derived` expression in 0.3. | Definition defect | Read |
| A6 | The definition's five `prevent` constraints carry five refusal sentences. The module says two of them (the property refusal and the reparenting refusal); "Add a playbook, role or inventory in a text editor.", "Delete the file or folder itself." and "Relationships come from the files' own directives." are sentences no user has read, for gestures the tool does not offer. Under FBL the binding's `readOnly` sentence is the refusal, so the definition and the binding would both state it. | Definition defect | Read |
| A7 | The `unmatchedHosts` message decides whether a play is unnamed by `!self.name.startsWith('play ')`, because a drawn play carries its display label (`play 2`) and not its written name. A play that is named `play the fool` would be reported as "A play". The module reads the written name. | Definition defect | Read |
| A8 | `unreadableYaml` joins every unreadable file into one finding, a workaround. In 0.3 it is the reader's `std.unparseable`, once per file, with a computed `code`. Its sentence is "'<path>' is not readable YAML: <reason>", and DISL 8.7 gives the message of `std.unparseable` one detail, `reason`: the path is in the finding's location and not readable in its message. | Language gap | Read |
| A9 | An inventory shows **one row per group** (id `ansible.group.` and the group's name, the name as label, "1 host" or "N hosts" as value) and one per variable folder. The definition shows one `table` field and one computed "Folders" row instead. A context-menu entry has `forEach`; a form item has not. | Language gap | Measured |
| A10 | "Used by" lists the distinct declaring files of a role's incoming relations. The definition's expression ends in `.filter(p, true)` and lists a file once per relation. DISL has `distinct()`. | Definition defect | Read |
| A11 | The module's wire ids are seven element types (`ansible/structure+playbook` to `ansible/structure+edge`) and the row ids `ansible.` and a name. The definition gives none. | Language gap, already ruled: wire ids stay an `x-` block (Peter, 2026-10-06). This definition gets an `x-ansible` block. | Read |
| A12 | **The order of findings.** The module reports unreadable files, then missing targets in the order the relations were derived (which interleaves `ansible.role-missing` and `ansible.dangling-import`), then unmatched hosts, then empty roles. DISL orders by rule, or with `constraints.order` by code and then by line. Every finding of this tool is in a different file, and a line orders nothing across files. | Language gap | Read |
| A13 | Double-click, Enter and Space reveal a node's file or folder in the explorer. DISL's `reveal` scrolls the canvas to an element; nothing opens an element's source in the host, and a tool has one `shortcut`. The definition names a plugin action for it. | Language gap | Read |
| A14 | The layout (ranks by import depth, every node of a rank at the rank's width, inventories in a band beneath) is none of DISL 0.3's three standard algorithms and stays a plugin. Its text width is the shared `TextMetric`, 14 by 0.55, which is DISL's `textMetric` of kind `average`. | Language gap (DISL D.2, open question 9) | Read |
| A15 | Two relations can have one id today: a play that names a role in `roles:` and again with `import_role` yields two relations whose ids are equal, and several root inventory files each yield the same variable folder. The canvas draws one. DISL would report `std.duplicateId`, give the later one an ephemeral id and draw both. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q3) | Read |
| A16 | `DislFinding` and `DislReaderFinding` carry a line and no file, and `ConstraintEvaluator` does not evaluate a rule's `location`. Every finding of this tool names its own file. | Runtime gap | Measured |
| A17 | The client's `compileNotation` has no `stub`. | Runtime gap | Measured |
| A18 | The viewport filter with its one hop of partners, the shared store, the selection resolver and the `.proto` payloads are the host's and stay code. Not a gap. | None | Read |

### B. The folder subject and the plugin contract against the module's reader

| # | Finding | Kind | Known |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | **Why the reading is a plugin.** A declared rule matches an entry of a file. A role is a folder under `roles/`, present with no file in it; its contents are counts of files in six subfolders and the existence of two more. A playbook is a file whose whole top level has a shape (a non-empty list of mappings only). A task file is drawn only when something includes it, a play only when its playbook has more than one. An inventory is YAML or, when it does not parse as YAML, INI with sections, `:children` and `:vars`. A target resolves by a path relative to the declaring file with `.` and `..` collapsed, or not at all when it holds `{{`. None of these is a selector or a slot. | None: FBL 11.5 says so | Read |
| B2 | **A folder is a fact, and the plugin is handed files.** `read` receives "the relative path and bytes of every file the file rules select". An empty `roles/x/` is a hollow role today and is reported as `ansible.empty-role`; an empty `meta/` makes a role not hollow; an empty `group_vars/` is a node with 0 files. None of them reaches a plugin that is given files only. The fixture hides it: `broken/roles/hollow/` holds a `README.md` because git stores no empty folder. | Language gap | Read |
| B3 | **Files that are counted are never opened today.** The reader lists `templates/`, `files/`, `handlers/`, `defaults/`, `vars/`, `group_vars/` and `host_vars/` and counts. Under the contract every selected file's bytes are read and handed over, a role's binary `files/` included. FBL has no file rule that yields a path and no bytes. | Language gap | Read |
| B4 | **Whose parser, whose words.** A file rule names a `family`, and FBL 10.3 reports a file "that cannot be read" as `std.unparseable`. Whether the host parses a plugin-read file by that family is not said. If it does, an INI `hosts` file and a broken `hosts.yml`, which the tool deliberately reads as INI and reports nothing for, gain a finding; and `ansible.unreadable-yaml` would carry the library parser's sentence where the tool promises "the parser's own message", today YamlDotNet's. A mapping that repeats a key is a third case: YamlDotNet refuses the file (as `timeline-disl-fbl`, finding B10, records for the timeline), FBL 7.4 reads it with a warning. The draft binding gives its file rules no `family`, so the plugin parses. | Language gap (ambiguity) | Read |
| B5 | **A folder that is not there, or holds nothing Ansible.** The tool opens it as an empty project with no finding and the sentence "Nothing here is laid out the way Ansible expects, so there is nothing to draw." FBL 10.3 makes a folder that does not exist, or does not satisfy `recognise`, an unreadable body with `std.unparseable`. `recognise` is required by the schema; an empty one recognises every folder, which is what the tool does, since a registration and never the content says a folder is an Ansible project. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q2) | Read |
| B6 | **Reading order.** FBL 4.1.3 and DISL 8.6 read a folder's files in the ordinal order of their relative paths. The module reads the root's playbooks, then `playbooks/`, then roles, then inventories. In the `broken` fixture `playbooks/deploy.yml` sorts before `site.yml` and the module reads it after. The order decides each play's colour index, the stacking inside a rank and the order of the payloads. Whether the order a plugin delivers its elements in is the reading order is not said. | Language gap | Read |
| B7 | **A relation without a target from a reader.** FBL 5.4 says "DISL relations always have both ends" and FBL 11.2 does not say a plugin may deliver a relation with no target. DISL 4.9 allows one since 0.2. The library's `FblElement.Target` is nullable, so the runtime is ahead of the text. | Language gap (FBL text) | Read |
| B8 | **The library has no folder body.** `PluginBody` is "a file body read by a persistence plugin": it hands the plugin one file with an empty path. `FolderSubject.Recognise` and `FolderSubject.Files` have no caller outside the library's tests. A library `Finding` has a file in its location; an `FblElement` has a line and a span and no file. `IPersistencePlugin` says of `watch` that no host calls it yet. | Runtime gap | Measured |
| B9 | **A stored position outlives its node today, and FBL removes it.** `RegistrationLayout.SetPosition` rewrites the block with every entry it read, and nothing in this module calls `Prune`. FBL 8.5 removes a stale entry at the next write and reports `fbl.stale-view-data`. For a folder subject a node is stale whenever its file is momentarily unreadable: a playbook saved half-edited loses its position at the next drag of any other node. FBL 7.3 keeps the last readable model for an unreadable body, and a folder subject has no such moment for one file. | Language gap, and a behaviour change to rule on (Q2) | Read; the absence of a caller is measured |
| B10 | **The layout block agrees.** Entries in ordinal order of their ids and numbers with at most three decimals are what `RegistrationLayout` writes and what FBL 8.3 says. The 34 stored keys are the module's ids as the plugin delivers them; 6 hold a `/`, which DISL's default id `pattern` refuses and the definition's widened one admits. | None, to hold by a real-file check | Measured |
| B11 | **A symbolic link.** The reader skips a folder that is a reparse point and reads a file that is one. FBL 10.2 follows neither. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q2) | Read |
| B12 | **Known quirks.** The companion's section 12 lists seven, among them: `hosts: ::1` is reported as unmatched because the pattern is split on `:`; a `Targets` relation shows "Declared in" as an empty file and its directive as `roles:`; a play's own `include_tasks` naming no file is silent. The definition mirrors the first. | Module defects, to rule on (Q4) | Recorded in the companion |

### C. Language gaps, as they would be reported to etalii-adp/etalii.adp

1. **FBL: folders in a folder subject** (B2). Candidate: a file rule with `kind: "folder"`, whose matches are handed to the plugin as paths.
2. **FBL: a file rule that yields the path and not the bytes** (B3). Candidate: `content: false` on a file rule.
3. **FBL: what `family` means on a file rule under a plugin reader**, and who reports a file that does not parse (B4).
4. **FBL: reading order of a plugin's elements** (B6), and **a relation without a target from a reader** (B7).
5. **FBL: a stale entry whose file is unreadable, not gone** (B9). Candidate: an entry is stale only when no file of the subject is reported unparseable, or after a read in which every file parsed.
6. **DISL: the file in the message of `std.unparseable`** (A8). Candidate: `detail.file`.
7. **DISL: one form row per item of a list** (A9). Candidate: `forEach` on a form item, as on a context-menu entry.
8. **DISL: the order of findings of a folder subject** (A12). Candidate: `constraints.order` by file in reading order before line, and a way to keep a declared list order across two codes.
9. **DISL: opening an element's source in the host, and a second shortcut** (A13).
10. **DISL: the ranked layout** (A14), which is D.2's open question 9.

These are candidates. Requirement 9 says they are recorded with their evidence and reported, and never worked around silently.

## Open questions

Each is put to the user as a selection. The option marked **(default)** is what this document is written against.

| # | Question | Options | Criteria affected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | How is the folder read? | **(default) A declared folder subject with a plugin reader**: the binding declares the files, the settle delay, read-only and the registration; a plugin that wraps today's reader and graph delivers the nodes and the relations, resolved. It follows FBL 11.5 and changes no reading. · **The plugin delivers directives only**, and the relations and their resolution become DISL derived relations: less code stays, and the host-pattern and path rules must first be shown expressible in CEL. · **Declared rules for the YAML, a plugin for the rest**: FBL names that outcome for one other tool and does not say how two readers share a body. · Other. | 4.1, 4.2, 6.1 |
| Q2 | What the languages would do that the tool does not today: `std.unparseable` for a folder that is not there (B5), a stored position removed while its file is unreadable (B9), `fbl.stale-view-data`, a linked file not read (B11). | **(default) Today's behaviour is kept** and each is switched off or reported as a gap: no new finding, no position lost, and each is raised afterwards as a small change of its own. · **Adopted now**, each named in the transcript's diff. · Other. | 3.3, 5.3 |
| Q3 | Two relations with one id (A15). | **(default) As today**: one is drawn, `std.duplicateId` is switched off, and the transcript shows it. · **Each repeat gets its own id** (`#2`, as DISL's derived relations do), is drawn and can be selected: a fix, with its own guard. · Other. | 3.3, 4.4 |
| Q4 | The seven known quirks (B12). | **(default) Kept byte for byte in this conversion**, each in the transcript, and each fixed afterwards on purpose with a test seen to fail first. · **Fixed now**, each named in the transcript's diff. · Other. | 1.2, 3.2 |
| Q5 | Is the client's canvas definition in scope? | **(default) Yes**: it is compiled from the bundled definition with `compileNotation`, with today's hand-written definition kept in a test as the oracle. · **No**: backend only. · Other. | 7 |

## Alignment with Product Vision

The product direction (2026-09-26) is that every tool is a markup definition interpreted by a core in each IDE, with code only where a definition cannot reach. This tool is the test of that sentence at its far end: its subject is a folder another ecosystem owns, it writes nothing, and most of its reading is code by FBL's own account. What the conversion can still take out of the module is everything a host does for every folder subject, and what it finds about the plugin contract is owed to the Helm chart, which FBL reads the same way. It follows `product.md`'s *Don't reinvent, integrate* and `structure.md`'s rule that a diagram type adds declarations and no core code: what the libraries lack (findings A16, B8) is added to the libraries for every tool.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: An oracle before any change

**User Story:** As the owner of the tool, I want what it answers today frozen before anything is converted, so that every later step is held to it.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the work starts THEN a parity transcript `Parity/ansible-structure.transcript.json` SHALL be generated from today's code and committed before any provider, reader or rule is changed: per folder, the payload of every element in delivery order with an unbounded viewport, the property rows of every node, of every relation and of an unknown id, the findings with code, severity, sentence, file, line and order, the selection text and path of every element, the empty toolbox answer, and the five refusal sentences of a move and of a property write.
2. The corpus SHALL be the four fixture trees, the module's `examples/`, the twelve projects under `src/examples/diagrams/ansible-structure/`, and **one new fixture for each finding marked Read in tables A and B** that a folder can show (A5, A7, A8, A12, A15, B2 to B7, B9, B11 and each quirk of B12), built in a temporary folder where git cannot hold it (an empty folder, a link), so that the finding either shows in the transcript or is struck from this document with the reason.
3. A test SHALL require today's code to reproduce the checked-in transcript byte for byte, and SHALL have been seen to fail against a deliberately changed sentence before it is trusted.
4. WHEN a later step changes the transcript THEN the change SHALL be one this document names (Q2 to Q4), regenerated on purpose, and the diff of the checked-in file SHALL be the review of it. Any other difference is a regression.

### Requirement 2: The definition, at DISL 0.3, bundled

**User Story:** As a tool engineer, I want one definition of the Ansible structure diagram that every host runs.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `definitions/diagrams/ansible-structure.dis` in etalii-adp/etalii.adp SHALL be rewritten at DISL 0.3 with the constructs findings A2 to A10 name in place of each workaround, with `language.origin` `ansible/structure`, and SHALL validate against the DISL schema in that repository's checks.
2. It SHALL declare `persistence.format` `fbl` with `binding` naming the module's binding (Requirement 4.1), ids as `derived` expressions that yield today's ids (finding A5), the plugin as the binding's reader and for the layout, and an `x-ansible` block mapping its element types and its form rows to the wire ids the module uses today (finding A11).
3. It SHALL state no sentence and no element type the tool has not got (findings A3, A6).
4. Its companion `ansible-structure.md` SHALL be rewritten to say what DISL 0.3 and FBL 0.2 cannot express, which is section C and whatever Requirement 9 adds, and nothing that they can.
5. The definition SHALL be bundled into `src/diagrams/ansible-structure/definition/` by `src/diagrams/tools/bundle-disl.sh`, never edited here, embedded in the backend project, held by a `BundledDefinition.Tests`, and SHALL load in `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl` with no diagnostic of severity error.

### Requirement 3: Rows, findings and refusals are derived

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want the property rows and the findings to come from the definition, so that changing the tool is changing one file.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The property rows of every node and relation SHALL be derived from the bundled definition through `FormDerivation`, mapped to the row ids of `x-ansible`, every row read-only with today's reason "Defined in <file>; edit it in a text editor." naming the file it names today, and a row with nothing to say absent. WHERE DISL cannot state the rows of an inventory (finding A9) THEN those rows SHALL come from module code named in the companion as standing in for the gap.
2. The five findings SHALL be derived by `ConstraintEvaluator` with the tool's codes (`ansible.role-missing`, `ansible.dangling-import`, `ansible.unmatched-hosts`, `ansible.unreadable-yaml`, `ansible.empty-role`), severities, sentences, files, lines and order. An expression target SHALL be reported by none, and the `unconventional` fixture SHALL report nothing.
3. No finding the tool does not give today SHALL appear (Q2, Q3), and WHERE DISL cannot state today's order (finding A12) THEN the order SHALL be kept by the code that hands the findings to the host, named as standing in for the gap.
4. The toolbox SHALL stay empty and no context action SHALL be offered, each asserted by a test; the refusal of a property write and of a reparenting move SHALL keep today's sentences, stated once (finding A6).
5. WHEN the derived answers are compared with the transcript of Requirement 1 THEN the rows, findings and payloads SHALL be byte-identical.
6. The hand-written providers' logic SHALL be kept in the test project as the oracle (`Parity/HandWrittenAnsible.cs`) and removed from the product code.

### Requirement 4: The folder is read as an FBL folder subject

**User Story:** As a user, I want every Ansible folder that opens today to open the same, selected and watched by the host and read by a plugin under FBL's contract.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The module SHALL own its binding, `backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.AnsibleStructure/ansible-structure.fbl`, embedded in the backend project: a folder body, file rules for what the reader reads today, `settle` 400, `readOnly` with the tool's sentence, and the plugin `net.etalii.adp.ansible.folder` as its reader (Q1). An example SHALL be offered to etalii.adp's `specifications/fbl/`.
2. The plugin SHALL implement `IPersistencePlugin.Read` over the files it is handed and SHALL deliver the nodes and relations `AnsibleProjectReader` and `AnsibleGraph` yield today, with today's ids, in today's order (finding B6), each with its file and line; it SHALL plan nothing, open no file and keep no state.
3. WHERE the contract cannot hand the plugin what the reader uses today (a folder, finding B2; a path without bytes, finding B3) THEN the plugin SHALL obtain it through a seam the design names, the companion SHALL name that seam as standing in for the gap, and `ZeroWrites.Tests` SHALL still pass unchanged.
4. A relation whose target is missing or is an expression SHALL be delivered without a target, kept, drawn as a stub with "(missing)" or "(expression)", and only the missing one reported (findings A3, B7).
5. A file that does not parse SHALL cost its own detail only and be reported as `ansible.unreadable-yaml` with YamlDotNet's message and line, once per file; an inventory that is not YAML SHALL be read as INI and reported by nothing (finding B4).
6. A folder that is not there, or holds nothing recognised, SHALL open empty with no finding and with today's empty-canvas sentence, stated by the definition's `canvas.empty` (finding B5, Q2).
7. A real-file check SHALL read every registered folder under `src/` through the binding and the plugin and compare ids per type with `AnsibleGraph`, and SHALL hold that every one of the 34 stored positions names an element.

### Requirement 5: Nothing of Ansible's is written, and positions stay

**User Story:** As an author who arranged a diagram, I want it to open where I left it, and my Ansible files untouched.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. No file of the folder other than the registration SHALL be written by any path, held by `ZeroWrites.Tests` run over the converted module.
2. Moving a node SHALL write the registration's `layout:` block as one undo step that restores the registration byte for byte, and the three move refusals (a relation, no history, no registration) SHALL keep today's sentences.
3. A stored position whose node is absent SHALL NOT be removed by a write and SHALL be applied again when the node returns (finding B9, Q2).
4. Every position stored in a registration today SHALL be applied after the conversion, with no registration rewritten to make it so.

### Requirement 6: What stays code, and why

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want the code that remains to be exactly what the languages cannot state, each piece with its reason.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The module SHALL keep: the plugin and the reader, YAML and graph code it wraps (finding B1), the layout (finding A14), the element mapper and the viewport filter, the selection resolver, the session, the `.proto` payloads, and the stand-ins of Requirements 3.1, 3.3 and 4.3.
2. `AnsibleRuleSet`, `AnsibleValidator`'s rules and the logic of `AnsibleContextPropertyProvider` SHALL leave the product code. `AnsibleProjectStore` and `AnsibleWatchedFolder` SHALL leave it when the library's folder body (Requirement 8.1) watches, settles and re-reads, and not before.
3. WHEN the conversion is complete THEN the companion SHALL list every remaining module class beside the gap or the host concern that keeps it, and a class with neither SHALL be removed.

### Requirement 7: The client

**User Story:** As a user, I want the canvas to look and behave as it does, drawn from the same definition the backend runs.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The client's canvas definition SHALL be compiled from the bundled definition with `parseDisl` and `compileNotation` (Q5), with what the library cannot read stated in a `NotationBindings`, and today's hand-written definition kept in a test as the oracle that draws the same markup for the corpus.
2. IF `compileNotation` cannot read something the definition states (the stub of finding A17, the forward bezier that loops round for a backward relation, the per-play tint by index, the dash of each of the five relation kinds) THEN it SHALL be added to the shared library for every module, named for its geometry, and SHALL NOT be written in this module.
3. The client SHALL keep one write, `moveElementTo`, no toolbox, no editable field and no draggable element, each still held by its test.
4. A `tests.md` entry SHALL cover in a real browser, in both themes: each node kind, a hollow role, the five relation kinds, a dynamic relation, a missing and an expression stub, the tint of plays of two playbooks, the empty-folder sentence, revealing a file by double-click, Enter and Space, a drag with its undo, and a change to a file of the folder appearing without a reload.

### Requirement 8: The library work this tool needs

**User Story:** As a maintainer of the shared libraries, I want each thing this tool needs added once, for every tool.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl` SHALL gain a folder body read by a plugin: it selects the files with `FolderSubject`, hands them to the plugin, watches, settles and reads again, never writes, and gives every element its file as a finding has one (finding B8). Each part SHALL be proven by a library test seen to fail first.
2. `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl` SHALL carry a finding's file, evaluate a rule's `location`, and support every construct of the rewritten definition that it does not support yet (finding A16); the design SHALL list which, from a load of the rewritten definition.
3. A language gap SHALL NOT be repaired in a library (Requirement 9), and no module name SHALL appear in a library change.

### Requirement 9: Gaps are recorded and reported, never tuned away

**User Story:** As the owner of DISL and FBL, I want every place the languages fall short reported back with its evidence.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every language gap found, the ten of section C and any the implementation adds, SHALL be recorded in the companion with the construct concerned, the evidence (a fixture or a test), and what would resolve it.
2. A gap SHALL NOT be closed by weakening a check, skipping a fixture, or stating in the definition or the binding something the tool does not do.
3. The delivery report SHALL list every gap as a candidate change for etalii-adp/etalii.adp, and every definition defect that was repaired.
4. WHEN a *read* finding of this document turns out not to occur THEN it SHALL be struck here with the fixture that shows it, as a small amendment.

### Requirement 10: Documentation, catalog and gates

**User Story:** As a reader of the repository, I want its pages to stay true through the conversion.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `src/diagrams/readme.md`'s list of modules with a `definition/` folder, `docs/creating-a-diagram-module.md`, `docs/diagram-module-client-api.md`, and `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/solution-structure.md` where a sentence becomes false SHALL be updated in the change that makes them so; the fixtures' readme SHALL name four trees.
2. `docs/tools.md`'s row for `ansible/structure` SHALL name this specification.
3. All four gates SHALL exit zero on every pull request of this specification, judged by captured exit codes, and a newly created worktree SHALL be built before a green gate is trusted about the bundled definition.
4. WHEN the tasks document is written THEN every acceptance criterion here SHALL be claimed by a task, established by diffing the two sets, and two traces SHALL be read back to their artefacts.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- The module ends as a definition, a binding, a plugin and the code Requirement 6.1 names. Library additions are named for what they do, never for this tool.
- The house rules apply: `src/.editorconfig`, no blocking call in an `async` method, `TestContext.Current.CancellationToken` in tests, no unneeded `using`, CRLF in the working tree; the fixture trees stay `-text`, and `.dis` and `.fbl` in the module follow what the hype cycle's have.

### Performance

- Opening and re-reading the largest folder of the corpus SHALL not be perceptibly slower than today. A file that is only counted today SHALL NOT be read into memory to be counted (finding B3).

### Reliability

- No folder that opens today opens differently. No file of Ansible's is written. No stored position is lost. Reading never throws on content, and one unreadable file costs only its own detail.
- Every test written for a finding is seen to fail against that finding before it is trusted.

### Usability

- Every sentence a user reads today is read unchanged, unless this document names the change.

## Out of scope

- Any edit of an Ansible file from the diagram. The tool is read-only, and this specification keeps it so.
- Any change to what the tool recognises or reports beyond the five questions above.
- Changing DISL or FBL. Gaps are reported (Requirement 9); a language change is etalii.adp's own specification.
- The other tools of the series, the Helm chart among them, which is the same shape and uses what Requirement 8 adds.
- The layout's algorithm and the viewport streaming model.

## Appendix: the binding, as drafted

A draft against FBL 0.2, shaped as `helm-chart.fbl`. It has no rules, no template and no header: the plugin reads, and a new diagram is a registration and nothing else. Two keys in it are **not FBL**: `x-folder` marks where the construct of finding B2 is needed, and `x-content` where that of finding B3 is. Both pass the schema, which admits `x-` keys, and mean nothing to a host. No file rule has a `family`, which is finding B4.

```json
{
  "fbl": "0.2",
  "bindings": {
    "ansible": {
      "title": "Ansible project folder",
      "claims": { "origins": ["ansible/structure"], "registrationOnly": true },
      "body": {
        "kind": "folder",
        "recognise": {},
        "files": [
          { "name": "annotations", "glob": "ansible.cfg", "x-content": false },
          { "name": "galaxy", "glob": "collections/requirements.y*ml", "x-content": false },
          { "name": "rootInventory", "glob": "inventory" },
          { "name": "rootHosts", "glob": "hosts" },
          { "name": "rootYaml", "glob": "*.y*ml" },
          { "name": "playbooks", "glob": "playbooks/*.y*ml" },
          { "name": "roles", "glob": "roles/*", "x-folder": true },
          { "name": "roleTasks", "glob": "roles/*/tasks/*.y*ml" },
          { "name": "roleMeta", "glob": "roles/*/meta/main.y*ml" },
          { "name": "roleFolders", "glob": "roles/*/*", "x-folder": true },
          { "name": "roleContents", "glob": "roles/*/*/*", "x-content": false },
          { "name": "environments", "glob": "inventories/*", "x-folder": true },
          { "name": "inventories", "glob": "inventories/*/*" },
          { "name": "variableFolders", "glob": "**/*_vars", "x-folder": true },
          { "name": "variables", "glob": "**/*_vars/*", "x-content": false }
        ],
        "ignore": [".git/**"],
        "settle": 400
      },
      "reader": { "plugin": "net.etalii.adp.ansible.folder", "version": "^0.1.0" },
      "readOnly": "An Ansible structure diagram shows the folder as it is and changes nothing in it. Edit the file this value comes from in a text editor.",
      "registration": { "createOnFirstPlacement": false }
    }
  }
}
```

Four things in it are unsettled and are the design's to close with fixtures: that `*.y*ml` also selects names the reader does not read (`x.yaaml`), which the plugin then passes over, where two globs per rule would be exact; that the first matching rule takes a file, so the order above matters; that the variable-folder globs select more folders than the two places the reader looks in; and that `.git/**` is ignored, where today a change under `.git` re-reads the folder.

## Appendix: the definition's persistence, plugin and wire ids, as drafted

The rest of the definition is the existing file brought to 0.3 (Requirement 2.1). No `typeMap` is needed: the plugin delivers the metamodel's own names.

```json
{
  "persistence": {
    "format": "fbl",
    "binding": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etalii-adp/etalii.adp.ide.standalone/develop/src/diagrams/ansible-structure/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.AnsibleStructure/ansible-structure.fbl#ansible",
    "ids": {
      "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'edge:' + self.source.id + '|' + self.kind + '|' + self.targetAsWritten",
      "pattern": "^\\S.{0,1023}$",
      "types": {
        "Playbook": { "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'playbook:' + self.path" },
        "Play": { "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'play:' + self.playbook.path + '#' + string(self.indexInPlaybook)" },
        "Role": { "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'role:' + self.name" },
        "TaskFile": { "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'taskfile:' + self.path" },
        "Inventory": { "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'inventory:' + self.path" },
        "VariableFolder": { "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'vars:' + self.path" },
        "Targets": { "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'edge:' + self.source.id + '|Targets|' + self.targetAsWritten + '|' + self.target.id" }
      }
    },
    "view": { "store": ["bounds"] }
  },
  "plugins": {
    "net.etalii.adp.ansible.folder": {
      "version": "^0.1.0", "provides": ["persistenceFormat", "layout", "action"], "required": true, "plans": []
    }
  },
  "x-ansible": {
    "elements": {
      "Playbook": "ansible/structure+playbook", "Play": "ansible/structure+play", "Role": "ansible/structure+role",
      "TaskFile": "ansible/structure+taskfile", "Inventory": "ansible/structure+inventory",
      "VariableFolder": "ansible/structure+vars", "AnsibleRelation": "ansible/structure+edge"
    },
    "properties": {
      "name": "ansible.name", "path": "ansible.path", "plays": "ansible.plays", "roles": "ansible.roles",
      "imports": "ansible.imports", "hosts": "ansible.hosts", "reaches": "ansible.inventories",
      "taskFiles": "ansible.tasks", "handlers": "ansible.handlers", "templates": "ansible.templates",
      "files": "ansible.files", "defaults": "ansible.defaults", "vars": "ansible.vars", "meta": "ansible.meta",
      "hollow": "ansible.hollow", "dependsOn": "ansible.dependencies", "usedBy": "ansible.used-by",
      "fileCount": "ansible.files", "declaredIn": "ansible.declared-in", "directive": "ansible.directive",
      "target": "ansible.target", "condition": "ansible.condition", "resolution": "ansible.resolution"
    }
  }
}
```

`self.kind` stands for the relation type's name (`UsesRole`, `ImportsPlaybook`, `IncludesTasks`, `DependsOn`) and is the design's to state, by a rule per type if DISL gives a type no name in CEL. The rows `ansible.group.` and `ansible.vars.` with a name are not in the map: they are finding A9. Whether a plugin's own ids or the `derived` expressions win when both are given is to be settled against DISL 11.5.1; they are written here so that the two agree and every host makes the same id.
